title: Frozen Tax-Free Allowance: About £776 a Year for Basic-Rate Taxpayers 🧊💷 #shorts
description:
About £776 a year: that's what the frozen tax-free Personal Allowance costs a basic-rate taxpayer.

In 2010-11 the Personal Allowance was £6,475. Kept in line with prices (ONS CPI, April 2010 to September 2026) that would be about £10,460 today, so until 2021 the allowance rose much faster than prices: it reached £12,570 in 2021-22. Then it was frozen, and it stays at £12,570 until April 2031.

Had it kept up with prices since April 2021, it would be about £16,450 now. That's £3,880 more of your pay taxed at 20%: about £776 a year.

Sources: legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2010/13/section/1 (2010-11 allowance) · legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2021/111 (2021-22 allowance) · gov.uk/income-tax-rates (2026/27) · gov.uk/government/publications/maintaining-income-tax-and-equivalent-national-insurance-contributions-thresholds-until-5-april-2031 · ONS CPI index D7BT: ons.gov.uk/economy/inflationandpriceindices/timeseries/d7bt/mm23

If you pay 40% tax, what would that same £3,880 cost you a year? Comment 👇
📩 Send this to the friend who says tax hasn't gone up.

Illustration only. "Kept up with prices" = the allowance scaled by the CPI index from the April it was set to September 2026 (the latest month). £776 = 20% of £3,880, for a basic-rate taxpayer earning at least £16,450 in England, Wales or Northern Ireland (Scotland's income tax bands differ). Ignores National Insurance and other thresholds. General education, not financial advice.

Music and sound effects: original, made for this channel.
